note: Tutorial hints, shown once each, in the order their moment comes. Triggers are checked by src/ui/hints.js.

hints.title: The crown of Temeria
hints.text: The realm lives on its own: carts on the roads, harvests, tempers. You steer it. Pause, 1x, 2x and 4x are at the top; drag to pan and pinch to zoom. Tap any town to see how it fares. The tabs along the foot (down the side when the phone lies flat) hold everything else, and tapping a meter at the top says why it moved.

hints.title: A town's card
hints.text: A town's card opens on its summary: people, fortunes, unrest, who holds it and its garrison, and the land it stands on. Works shows each of its spaces (the river, the fields, the town square) and what stands in each, with how well it stands: tap one to mend it. Military holds its garrison and recruiting, People its peoples and faiths.

hints.title: A decision
hints.text: Envoys, petitions, lords' demands, war and news from the realm wait under Court, Decisions, with a badge on the tab. Each is answered right there in the list. Leave one and the choice marked is taken for you when its time runs out.

hints.title: The first accounts
hints.text: On the first of every month the accounts are drawn up. Treasury, Ledger shows every crown that came in and went out, and which towns earned and cost the most. A purse that runs dry can borrow from the dwarven banks, at a price in Authority.

hints.title: Your strongest lever
hints.text: Court, Laws changes taxes, order, faith and more. Every decree costs Authority and pleases some groups while angering others: tap a law to see who. The realm's mood sits at the top.

hints.title: Hunger
hints.text: Somewhere the stores are empty. Grain moves from full barns to empty ones by itself, but cities cannot feed themselves. Fields, watermills and fisheries in good repair are the cure: mend the ones that are broken.

hints.title: Into the red
hints.text: The treasury has gone below zero. The bankers charge about one crown in a hundred each month, and the lords' respect for the crown drains while the debt stands; deep in debt, the tax farmers squeeze the towns and unrest rises. Treasury, Ledger shows every crown in and out, line by line, and what each place earned and cost: look there for what to cut and what is worth mending.

hints.title: The great houses
hints.text: Five houses hold land of the crown and keep their own soldiers (Court, Great houses). Their loyalty rises with favours and falls with grievances. Let it collapse with your Authority and they will depose you.

hints.title: Raiders
hints.text: A village has been raided. Raids come from things on the map: bandit camps and their bands on the roads, beasts from their lairs, Scoia'tael out of the woods and war parties over the border. Garrisons defend their own walls; to stop raids at the source, send companies after them from Military, Threats, set them patrolling the roads, or hire witchers for the beasts.

hints.title: Authority is slipping
hints.text: With little Authority you cannot pass laws or bend the lords. It recovers each month, faster when the houses are content and the court impresses them.

hints.title: War drums
hints.text: A neighbour is gathering an army. Realms that dislike the crown, or smell weakness, attack. Better relations, a strong Authority, or an army of your own may change their minds.

hints.title: At war
hints.text: Military, War raises armies: a levy from crown garrisons, the lords' men, and hired companies, mustered at a town you tap on the map. Give each army an order and a stance and its marshal does the marching. Tap an army on the map for its card.

hints.title: Your army
hints.text: Hold a place and the army meets any enemy that comes near. Besiege a town and it starves or storms it, then holds it. Raid a realm and it plunders unwalled places, then comes home. Tap Hold or Besiege, then tap the place on the map: the banner shows what you would face before you confirm.

hints.title: A town lost
hints.text: An enemy holds a Temerian town: it pays the crown nothing and its lord is furious. Retake it by siege, or make peace. A peace where each keeps what it holds gives it away for good, but it remains a just cause for a later war.

hints.title: Look closer
hints.text: Pinch to zoom in on a town. Up close you see its houses, workshops, fields and walls, with smoke rising and workers going out to the fields. Every works its land gives it stands in its place, and the town spreads as it grows.

hints.title: Trade routes
hints.text: Treasury, Trade routes opens crown routes between towns and cities, at home or in a friendly neighbour: tap the far end on the map and see what it would earn before you pay. A route earns each month from both towns' size and fortunes, the length of the haul and safe roads; patrols protect it and war closes it. Market halls and guildhalls let you run more.

hints.title: Gold in the hills
hints.text: Old gold workings lie flooded near Carreras, Zavada, Razwan, Petrelsteyn and Rissberg. Rebuild the gold mine from the town's Works and it pays the treasury every month until the seam runs out. Others may hide elsewhere in the hills: send prospectors from a hill town's card. Gold draws miners and dwarves, but also bandits and greedy neighbours.

hints.title: Mending, not building
hints.text: The crown does not build: every place already has the works its land gives it. They wear with use, and raids, armies, storms and fire break them. A broken works asks the crown at court: rebuild it (whole, but idle while the masons work), patch it (cheaper, but it may give way again) or leave it (free, but the place goes without and remembers).

hints.title: Something in the wilds
hints.text: A threat has been sighted: a bandit camp, a beast's lair, a commando or a war party. Tap it on the map, or open Military, Threats, and send the nearest suitable company in one tap, with the odds in plain words. Beasts are best left to a witcher. Companies are recruited from a town's card under Military; give them orders by tapping the map: hunt, patrol a road, hold a station, or stand ready to answer whatever is sighted near them.

hints.title: The kingdom's hands
hints.text: Realm, Labour shows where the kingdom's hands work: the fields from spring to harvest, the woods and turf cuts for winter fuel, the mines, the boats, the workshops, the masons and the levies. Move them five in a hundred at a time. Before first frost, call the winter turn, or the field hands sit idle while the woodpiles run low.

topics.title: Finding your way
topics.text: Five tabs hold the realm: Realm (the dashboard and every place), Court (decisions, laws, the great houses, faith), Treasury (the ledger, trade routes, mines and industry), Military (companies, threats, garrisons, war) and Diplomacy (neighbouring realms, spies and embassies, envoys). Each reopens where you left it. Chronicle, Help and saves are under the three dots at the top.

topics.title: The panel
topics.text: On a phone held upright the panel is a sheet you can drag by its title bar: just the title, half the screen, or all of it. Tapping the map lowers it to its title bar rather than closing it, and a tap on the title brings it back as it was. The back arrow, or your phone's back gesture, returns to the screen before. Held flat, the panel sits beside the map and stays open.

topics.title: The four meters
topics.text: Treasury is coin in hand; Granary the food in every store; Authority the crown's grip on the realm, spent by decrees and the lords; Stability the realm's calm, from the unrest of every place. Tap one to see what moved it.

topics.title: Picking on the map
topics.text: Orders that need a place or a target (a hunt, a patrol, a station, a trade route, an army's march, where to muster) are given by tapping the map. A banner says what to tap; once you tap, it shows the odds or what it would earn, and you confirm or tap elsewhere.

topics.title: What cannot wait
topics.text: War declared on Temeria, a siege of one of our towns, a rebellion and a deposition raise a red banner across the top. Tap it to go straight there. Everything else waits quietly in the Court inbox.

topics.title: Long press
topics.text: Hold a finger on the map for half a second, until the ring under it fills. On one of your towns it offers Build, Recruit, Garrison, Trade route and Open card; on a company or army, its orders; on a threat, sending the nearest company. On anything foreign it says what is known, and on open land what's here: the ground, whose land, the nearest place and how dangerous it is. Hold a row in a list for a quick look without leaving it.

topics.title: Moving about the map
topics.text: Drag to pan, and flick to send the map gliding. Pinch to zoom, double tap open land to zoom in, and tap with two fingers to zoom out.

topics.title: Install and play offline
topics.text: Add the game to your home screen from the browser's menu (Share, then Add to Home Screen on an iPhone). It opens full screen, starts at once and plays without a connection. When a new version is ready, a small prompt offers to restart. Switching away saves and pauses the reign.

topics.title: The North and the lands beyond
topics.text: Eleven realms border our dealings: Redania, Kaedwen, Aedirn, Mahakam, Cidaris, Kerack, Brokilon, Verden, Brugge, Sodden and Cintra. Further off lie the lands beyond (Kovir, Poviss, Hengfors, Lyria and Rivia, Dol Blathanna, Angren, Nazair, Mag Turga, Toussaint, Tir Tochair, Metinna, Korath and Skellige), drawn lighter: the crown knows their towns from its maps and nothing more. Camps and lairs over the border are that realm's to deal with; our companies and witchers do not cross after them.

topics.title: Audiences with rulers
topics.text: Tap a ruler's portrait on the Diplomacy tab, or Audience on their realm card or capital, to meet them. Trade lays a deal on the table and shows their verdict as you add things; What would they accept? asks for their price. Diplomacy holds gifts, envoys, spies and demands; Alliance holds treaties; War holds the reason you give and the terms you can demand first. Their mood shows its reasons; their trust remembers whether Temeria keeps its word, and breaking a treaty costs trust in every court.
